issues.description: Method messageOnRide: The problem statement (UML and textual description) and the template Main expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() that returns a String (used as r.messageOnRide()). The solution repository instead defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements messageOnRide(int speed) in Pig and Seal. This introduces an extra int parameter in the solution that conflicts with the method signature implied by the problem and the template, causing confusion and compilation mismatch when using the template Main or following the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across problem, template, and solution. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the UML and template by modifying Rideable to declare String messageOnRide(); then update Pig and Seal to implement public String messageOnRide() (no parameters) and return strings formatted as "Riding on Pig [name]" and "Riding on Seal [name]" respectively (removing the speed parameter and mph wording). Ensure any example calls in Main remain r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. Alternatively, if the exercise should include a speed parameter, update the problem statement and template Main to require and call messageOnRide(int speed) and document the parameter; but prefer the first option to preserve the UML and current template usage.

issues.description: Concept: the ride action method for rideable animals. Problem statement (UML and textual description) and the template expect a no-argument method named messageOnRide() that returns a String (UML: Rideable.messageOnRide():String; textual instructions: messageOnRide() should return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). Template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. The solution repository instead defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements messageOnRide(int speed) in Pig and Seal, embedding speed in the returned string. This changes the method signature (adds an int parameter) and the expected return content, preventing students from mapping the required no-arg messageOnRide() to the provided solution interface and implementations and causing compilation/signature mismatch if they follow the problem/template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the messageOnRide signature consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem/template by updating Rideable to declare String messageOnRide(); and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() with no parameters, returning the expected string format "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (e.g., "Riding on Pig Doodle"). Alternatively (less preferred) update the problem statement and template to document messageOnRide(int speed) and update examples and tests to include the speed parameter.
